evidence.supports: The only May 2026 council action on the five-year moratorium was direction to advertise a public hearing; no adoption item.
evidence.quote: Discussion/Direction: Advertise for Public Hearing for Approval of Ordinance 26-__ Establishing a Temporary Five-Year Moratorium on New Large-Scale Data Center Development

evidence.supports: On 2026-07-14 the council took up a draft permanent ban resolution (discussion/direction), not a moratorium.
evidence.quote: Discussion/Direction: Draft Resolution Adopting a Data Center Ban in Calipatria City Limits.

evidence.supports: The 3-2 vote advanced a permanent ban that still needed a second reading and final adoption.
evidence.quote: The proposal must return to the City Council for a formal second reading and final adoption before the permanent ban takes effect.

evidence.supports: 2026-08-11 agenda has no data center ban introduction or adoption item (only a county Data Center Advisory Committee report).
2026-08-25 agenda: the only ordinance introduced is Ordinance No. 01-26 (ADUs); no data center ban, contrary to the tracker's 'final adoption Aug 26'.
evidence.quote: Public Hearing: Introduction of an Ordinance No. 01-26 Amending text in the City of Calipatria Zoning Code as it relates to Accessory Dwelling Units

evidence.supports: 2026-09-08 agenda: second reading of Ordinance No. 01-26 (ADUs) only; no data center ban.
2026-09-22 agenda: no data center ban item.
The mayor says staff have not brought the permanent ban back to council.
evidence.quote: Data center ban: Requests to present a permanent data center ban to the council have not been fulfilled.

decisions.notes: REMOVE: no moratorium was ever adopted and none is still proposed. The five-year urgency moratorium got only a 2026-05-12 direction to advertise a hearing; the council then dropped it for a PERMANENT ban (2026-07-14 3-2 direction on a draft ban resolution), which is out of scope as a ban proposal. The tracker (aigridwatch) is wrong on adoption: the council meets 2nd/4th Tuesdays (Aug 11 and Aug 25, not Aug 12/26), and the Aug 11, Aug 25, Sep 8 and Sep 22 agendas carry no ban ordinance (the only 2026 ordinance, No. 01-26, is about ADUs). It is right that the live proposal is a permanent ban. If the ban is adopted later it still falls outside the inventory.
